description:
Converts annotated CDSs into annotated protein sequences

Takes a domainator-annotated genbank file 
Creates peptide genbank or fasta files with the domainator annotations from the CDSs found in the original
genbank file

By default, extracts peptides from all CDSs in the genbank file.

If any criteria are supplied, then only peptides from CDSs that meet the criteria will be extracted.

Criteria are combined with the following logic:
    (all OR target_CDSs OR target_domains OR unannotated OR search_hits) AND (target_contigs OR strand)

parameters.name: Output
parameters.help: the name of the output genbank file.

parameters.name: Databases
parameters.help: Consider only domains from these databases when filtering by domain. default: all databases.

parameters.name: Unannotated
parameters.help: extract peptides from CDSs with no domain annotations.

parameters.name: Annotation Type
parameters.help: Which annotations to select peptides by. With domain_search, the search hits are extracted. domainator: domain annotations (from domainate). domain_search: best-hit annotations (from domain_search).

parameters.name: Strand
parameters.help: Only extract peptides from CDSs on the specified strand.

parameters.name: Invert
parameters.help: Invert the CDS selection criteria. i.e. return peptides from CDSs that don't match the CDS selection criteria. (Only applies to CDS selection, not contig selection)

parameters.name: Cdss
parameters.help: only look for peptides on cdss with these names

parameters.name: Cdss File
parameters.help: only look for peptides on cdss with names listed in this text file.

parameters.name: Keep Name
parameters.help: by default, extracted regions will be renamed to note their original coordinates and whether they were reverse complemented. Set this option to keep contigs with their original names. WARNING: if you aren't careful, this can easily result in duplicate names.

parameters.name: Name Field
parameters.help: The CDS qualifier to preferentially use as the name of the peptide. If not supplied, then qualifiers will be checked in order of: ["protein_id", "gene_id", "locus_tag", "gene"]

parameters.name: Evalue
parameters.help: the evalue cutoff for domain annotations to be put onto the new genbank file

parameters.name: Fasta Out
parameters.help: Write the records to this FASTA file. Use - for standard output.

advanced_parameters.name: Contigs
advanced_parameters.help: only look for peptides on contigs with ids in this list. Additive with --contigs_file. default: all contigs.

advanced_parameters.name: Contigs File
advanced_parameters.help: only look for peptides on contigs with ids listed in this file (one per line). Additive with --contigs. default: all contigs.

advanced_parameters.name: Domains
advanced_parameters.help: Only extract peptides containing these domains

advanced_parameters.name: Domains File
advanced_parameters.help: text file containing names of domains, where peptides containing these domains will be extracted.

advanced_parameters.name: Partial
advanced_parameters.help: Which CDSs to extract peptides from, by fragment status. include: all. exclude: skip fragments. only: only fragments. A CDS is a fragment if its location has '<' or '>', or it has a /partial qualifier. A protein record is a fragment if it has a UniProt ' (Fragment)' or MGnify 'FL=0' header, a 'Flags: Fragment' definition or NON_TER features (UniProt text entries), or a CDS/Protein feature with '<' or '>' spanning it. Not affected by --invert.
